headline: Nobel Prize for economics awarded to Hall and Woodford for work on ‘smoothing’ crises

members.title: Americans Robert Hall and Michael Woodford win economic Nobel
members.lead: American economists Robert Hall and Michael Woodford were awarded the Nobel economics prize Monday for their work into how monetary and fiscal policy can help stabilise fluctuations in the economy. The two were recognised "for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation", the jury at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said.

members.title: Nobel Prize for economics awarded to Hall and Woodford for work on ‘smoothing’ crises
members.lead: US economists developed models that help central bankers and finance ministers to stabilise their economies Business live – latest updates Two US economists have won the 2026 Nobel economics prize for their work developing models that help central bankers and finance ministers to stabilise their countries, avoiding long recessions and runaway inflation. Robert Hall of Stanford University, California, and Michael Woodford of Columbia University, New York, were recognised for developing the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation”, giving policymakers better tools to smooth out the peaks and troughs of their economies.
